candidate_relations.reason: Cockayne-Touraine type does not preserve the required pruriginosa subtype despite belonging to the dystrophic EB family.
Porphyria cutanea tarda is an acquired porphyrin disorder and does not match the COL7A1-associated pruriginosa phenotype.
Lichen simplex chronicus may resemble the chronic pruritic lichenified plaques but does not account for dermoepidermal separation, milia, and the COL7A1 variant.
Dermatitis describes a broad clinical manifestation and omits the inherited dystrophic blistering disorder and pruriginosa subtype.
Epidermolysis bullosa pruriginosa is a genodermatosis, but this label lacks the specific disease, subtype, and COL7A1-associated dystrophic blistering context.
Dermatitis herpetiformis is not the COL7A1-associated dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa pruriginosa diagnosed here.
The COL7A1 variant supports the diagnosis but states only a genetic finding, not epidermolysis bullosa pruriginosa itself.
Epidermolysis bullosa simplex is distinct from the COL7A1-associated dystrophic EB pruriginosa subtype.
Hallopeau-Siemens type is not the required pruriginosa subtype and typically has a different generalized severe phenotype.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Alternative severe dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa subtype

candidate_relations.reason: Hyperkeratosis may accompany lichenified plaques but is not the final inherited blistering diagnosis.
Lichen sclerosus does not explain the COL7A1-associated dermoepidermal separation and milia characteristic of dystrophic EB pruriginosa.
Dominant dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa is compatible with the heterozygous COL7A1 finding but omits the required pruriginosa phenotype/subtype.
Psoriasis does not account for the inherited COL7A1-associated blistering, dermoepidermal separation, erosions, and milia.
Dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa inversa is a distinct subtype and conflicts with the required pruriginosa diagnosis and localized shin phenotype.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Alternative dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa distributional subtype

candidate_relations.reason: Dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa pruriginosa is the full name of epidermolysis bullosa pruriginosa and matches the pruritic pretibial lesions, milia, separation, and COL7A1 variant.
